open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock read scope
open_points.text: “the wall clock gives the instant … one reading per request … (no cache, no local time, no second reading, no arithmetic)” conflicts with “An operation reads the clock once”, `system_clock` providing “One wall reading per call”, the audit writer taking `occurred_at` when it appends, and “each read at the same point of the same operation.”
open_points.question: Does “request” mean an HTTP request, a use-case operation, or one call to `system_clock.utc_now`; and does `audit_writer.append_audit` take an independent wall reading or reuse the enclosing request/operation instant?
options: One wall instant is shared by every operation and audit append in an HTTP request.
Each use-case operation calls `utc_now` once, and the audit writer takes its own independent call when appending.
Each use-case operation has one instant, but the audit writer reuses its caller’s instant despite the stated append-time exception.
open_points.default_guess: Treat each use-case operation as taking one `utc_now` reading and let the audit writer take its own reading, preserving the stated existing moments and audit exception.

witness.initial: An active administrator session expires at instant T, and a project mutation request reaches the API immediately before T.
events: `staff_identity.resolve_staff_session` evaluates the session just before T and returns a `StaffActorContext`.
After T, `authorization_guard` performs the flow’s required valid-session check before the mutation.
outcomes: If one wall instant is shared for the HTTP request, the session remains valid for the guard and the mutation proceeds.
If each operation or `utc_now` call receives a fresh reading, the guard observes `now >= T` and rejects the request with the concealed authentication failure.
witness.observer: The administrator sees mutation success versus HTTP 401.
